a-note-for-grown-ups-and-kids-reading-to.plain: This book is for kids and grown-ups to read together. It names tricky things people do, and it gives you simple things to say and do so you feel safe and brave.

the-memory-mixer-upper.plain: Sometimes a person says something never happened, even when you know it did. Your memory is real. You can say what you remember and tell a grown-up you trust.

the-blame-game.plain: Sometimes a person does something wrong and then says it is your fault. You do not have to carry their choice. Each person owns what they chose to do.

the-guilt-gripper.plain: Sometimes a person makes you feel bad on purpose so you will do what they want. Saying no is okay, and a real friend still likes you when you do.

the-super-fast-best-friend.plain: Sometimes a new friend says you are their best friend really fast. Real friendship grows slowly, like a plant. It is okay to take your time.

the-silent-freeze-out.plain: Sometimes a person stops talking to you to make you feel bad. Being ignored is hard, but it is not your job to fix it by giving up what you need.

the-whisper-game.plain: Sometimes a person passes along whispers and rumors to make friends fight. You can go and talk to the friend yourself, kindly and face to face.

the-hot-and-cold-game.plain: Sometimes a friend is super nice one day and mean the next. That mix-up can make you try harder and harder. A good friend is kind most of the time.

the-jealousy-juggler.plain: Sometimes a person uses jealous feelings to pull friends apart. You can have more than one friend, and friends do not have to compete.

the-comparison-trap.plain: Sometimes a person compares you to others to make you feel small. You are not a contest. You can be proud of you.

the-drama-creator.plain: Sometimes a person starts fights and big feelings just to get attention. You can stay calm, step back, and not join the drama.

the-peer-pressure-pusher.plain: Sometimes friends push you to do something you do not want to do. You can say no and still belong. Real friends respect your no.

the-body-copycat.plain: Sometimes a person copies how you move and talk so you feel close to them fast. Copying is not the same as caring. Watch what they do over time.

the-compliment-stealer.plain: Sometimes a person says nice things so you will owe them something. A real compliment is a gift with no strings attached.

the-secret-whisperer.plain: Sometimes a person says, don't tell anyone. Some secrets are not safe to keep. You can always tell a grown-up you trust, and you will not be in trouble.

the-fear-spreader.plain: Sometimes a person scares you so you will stay quiet or do what they say. Being scared is a sign to tell a grown-up you trust right away.

the-group-up.plain: Sometimes a group decides to leave one kid out, and nobody says who started it. You can be the one who says, come sit with us.

the-best-friend-trap.plain: Sometimes a friend acts like you are amazing, then suddenly acts like you are nothing. Up and down like a roller coaster is not how good friends feel.

the-tricky-players-playbook.plain: Some very tricky people use many tricks together and never seem to stop. When that happens, you do not have to handle it alone. Get a grown-up to help.

the-unfair-clubhouse.plain: Some groups have unfair rules that say you can only belong if you obey. A good group lets you ask questions, have other friends, and say no.

the-internet-ghost.plain: Online, a person might pretend to be someone they are not. If someone you met online asks for secrets, pictures, or to meet, tell a grown-up you trust.

the-social-media-maze.plain: Online, people can pile on, leave someone out, or say mean things fast. You can stop, take a breath, stay kind, and show a grown-up.

the-mean-voice-in-your-head.plain: Sometimes the mean words other people said get stuck inside your head. You can talk back to that voice with kind, true words about yourself.

the-protectors-power-ups.plain: All your Power-Ups in one place: the things you can say and do when a trick happens. Practice them, so they are ready when you need them.
aka: what to say to a bully

the-power-of-forgiveness.plain: Forgiving someone can help your heart feel lighter. It does not mean you have to forget, or let the hurt happen again.

the-friendship-architect.plain: Good friendships are built step by step, with kindness, honesty, and trust. This mission shows you how to build friendships that feel good.

quiet-heroes.plain: Being brave can be small and quiet, like sitting with a kid who is alone. You can help in ways that feel safe for you.

the-kindness-chain-reaction.plain: One kind thing can spread from person to person, like a chain. When you are kind, you help kindness grow.

the-final-level.plain: You made it to the end! This is a look back at everything you learned, and all the ways you can keep being a Playground Protector.

the-power-up-master-guide.plain: Every Power-Up from the book in one place, so you can find the right thing to say or do fast.

the-tricksters-glossary.plain: A word list of all the tricks in the book, with simple meanings, so you can name what is happening.

the-feeling-words-index.plain: Twenty-eight feeling words to help you say how you feel. When you can name a feeling, it gets easier to handle.

the-big-ideas-on-one-page-each.plain: The biggest ideas from the book, each one short and simple, for a quick reminder any time.

the-playground-protectors-pledge.plain: A promise you can make: to be kind, to be brave, to trust yourself, and to ask for help when you need it.

resources.plain: For grown-ups: places to get more help for bullying, online safety, serious family situations, and children's mental health.
